Crop burning upwind: NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections of the last 3 days within 300 km, weighted toward the forecast wind direction; it explains a smog day, it does not change it.
Dispersion uses the ventilation index (boundary-layer height × wind) and morning inversions; it flags smog-trapping weather regardless of emissions.

v.method:
v91.17.283.13 · RIVER LINK BY DRAINAGE (audit B4 item 1). Builds data/river-link.json.

Replaces the district inheritance of a gauge's main-river level (data/river-reach-units.json: every tehsil of a district listed under a
gauge took that gauge's level wherever it lay) with a link along the river itself:
  river     the main-stem centre line of each named river (data/pk-rivers.json: OpenStreetMap waterway=river, main stem by the longest
            shortest path, ordered downstream)
  gauge     each river forecast point of data/flood.json is placed on its own river's line (nearest vertex: chainage in km from the
            upstream end); its REACH is the stretch of that line nearer to it than to the next gauge up or down the same river (midpoints
            in chainage); the first gauge's reach starts at the line's upstream end, the last one's ends at the confluence or the sea
  tehsil    linked to a gauge when that gauge's reach passes through or along the tehsil, within half a river-model cell (0.025 deg,
            the resolution of the 0.05 deg model the level comes from): rivers are often the tehsil boundary. A tehsil no gauged reach
            touches has no river level, whatever its district
  check     the national channel review (store/static/flood_risk/false_channels.json: GloFAS v4 channels with no river on the ground by
            MODIS 2002-2024 floods and JRC GSW / Landsat water, OSM canals excluded) is applied as a mask: a reach cell it disputes is
            dropped (none on the ten perennial rivers, per the review); per tehsil the disputed and the ungauged channel cells are counted
            as facts (why a desert tehsil with a GloFAS 'channel' gets no river level)
Height above the river (HAND, data/hand-tehsil.json) is applied at serve time (server/api/riverlink.mjs), not here.

rainCalibration.label: chance of rain
rainCalibration.basis: frequency matching of the deterministic model grid (0-24 h lead) to IMERG: tau_day is the grid day total whose exceedance frequency equals the IMERG wet-day share (>= 1.0 mm) over tehsil anchor points of the group (floor 0.1 mm); tau_hour is the grid hourly amount exceeded with frequency (IMERG wet-day share) x (wet hours per wet day at AGN MACH gauges) / 24. A member above tau counts as rain; the chance is the share of members above it. No station record enters the thresholds.
rainCalibration.source: Precipitation reference: NASA GPM IMERG (Huffman et al.), via NASA GES DISC / SERVIR ClimateSERV.

rule.hourly: pWet = P(1 h ≥ 0.1 mm) = the share of members whose grid cell carries a trace (not printed as a chance); pRain = the chance of rain: P(1 h ≥ τ) with τ frequency-matched to IMERG satellite rain (rainCalibration, v91.17.70), null when no calibration exists; pRainDay likewise with the day threshold, except in the mountain liquid-rain domain, where it is the station-calibrated day chance (pRainDayBasis, rainDayCalibration, v91.17.71); pGt1, pGt5 likewise; P50/P90 of the hourly member totals
rule.daily: ex = P(R24 ≥ k) for k in 1/5/10/25/50/100 mm; any trigger total is read by log-linear interpolation between the two nearest k
rule.verdict: single run, ensembles disagree: served total ≥ trigger and P < 0.15; ensemble watch: served total < trigger and P ≥ 0.40

thermal.method: WBGT: Liljegren et al. 2008 (globe and natural wet-bulb solved from their energy balances; 10 m wind scaled to 2 m by the Pasquill-Gifford profile). Tmrt: Di Napoli et al. 2020 / ERA5-HEAT from the provider shortwave (global, direct, DNI); longwave estimated (Prata 1996 emissivity, Crawford-Duchon cloud term), surface = air temperature, surface albedo fixed at 0.20 everywhere (the measured per-place, per-season albedo of v199 was retired in v91.17.277: no shipped grid holds it). UTCI: Bröde et al. 2012 polynomial on 2 m T, Tmrt, 10 m wind, vapour pressure. Ported from ECMWF thermofeel 2.3.0 and verified against it (max 0.05 °C, 2,000 cases).
thermal.albedo: fixed 0.20 (no measured albedo at this place)
thermal.caveat: the wind is the model 10 m wind at grid scale; the radiation is modelled; WBGT is the environmental value only: ISO 7243 reference values depend on workload, acclimatisation and clothing (no rest schedule is derived); not a site assessment

freezing.method: FDH_τ = Σ max(0, τ − T_served,t) · Δt on the served, corrected temperature (MOS, elevation, all hours)
freezing.caveat: τ is the asset’s own threshold; 0 °C is a freeze-exposure default, not a design value

wind.method: q = ½ρV², ρ = P_d/(R_d T) + P_v/(R_v T) from the model surface pressure, temperature and humidity; V = 10 m gust
wind.caveat: wind load screening, not a structural check: height, exposure, terrain, pressure coefficients and dynamic response belong to the applicable standard

snow.method: q_s = 0.00980665 × SWE_mm would need a snow depth this build can defend; the model snow depth measured 310 cm against 36 cm observed at the check station (correlation −0.10) and is not used as an input anywhere in this build
